what: pale hide tents on cypress platforms on a mud bank, five wardens living there (Ree-An-Wo's low decks, no rooms)

said.words: Pale hide tents on cypress platforms on a mud bank and a woven weir across the creek, with a log walk along its top and long grey moss draped on its fences over the water.
Five wardens live here in hide tents on cypress platforms beside a woven weir and a landing, running the eel and fish traps that supply Jal-Veesa's market.
Its main source, Ree-An-Wo (King of the Murkmire), is an Argonian camp of hide tents and hide fences on cypress platforms and walkways round a pool, with no rooms to enter.
Reed-Sill Weir is built from Ree-An-Wo's low cypress decks on the shore of the pool and the landing among them, set on the creek's mud bank.
Ree-An-Wo's own tents stand on its watch towers, which Reed-Sill does not take.
The pale hide tents on Reed-Sill's decks are Black Marsh's own, and Ree-An-Wo's fire and cooking pot are laid beside the landing.
Reed-Sill keeps only a few low decks beside its weir on the creek.

why: three pale Black Marsh hide tents on five low cypress decks of Ree-An-Wo's kit, five bedrolls; the source's watch-tower tents not taken

what: history, who holds the weirs, where the place lies and what other places take of the same source

said.words: The weirs date back to before the Dunmer and are kept by the Veesa-Teeleel wardens of Jal-Veesa.
Reed-Sill Weir is a Veesa-Teeleel weir on the creek north-east of Gandranen.
The Sedge-Wardens hold the creeks of Barsaebica and sell their catch at Jal-Veesa; an outpost on a creek in their country is one of their weirs.
Veesa-Teeleel families take turns at the weir, sent in rotation from Jal-Veesa, whose market the traps feed.
Karsh-Naal Camp takes the whole camp with its watch towers, its Xanmeer ruin and its dark tents, and dresses it with bone totems, and Ayiin is rebuilt there in squared stone.

why: history, directions to other places, rotation of families from Jal-Veesa and Karsh-Naal's own use of the source: nothing to build at this place
